A formalization study

Spirit Island in Turn

Can the rules of a large, heavily expanded board game be written so that each Turn rule matches one rulebook sentence, and every expansion, card and spirit is added without rewriting what came before?

Summary Reading Turn The base rules First extensions Extension patterns All spirits Language findings What to change Appendix

Summary

Mostly yes, if the base is written for it. All 37 spirits' special rules were written as separate files on top of one base slice. Of 67 rules, none needed rewriting the base except three (two spirits). Nineteen are partial: the core of the rule works, but some clause needed a feature Turn doesn't have.

The additions only went in cleanly where the base exposed the right hook: a named view for each noun the rulebook uses, a summed relation for each quantity, its own episode for each verb, and a name for each choice. Where the base hadn't done that, the addition needed a base change or stayed partial.

The most common problems were not about individual rules:

  • Simultaneity. Rules that fire at the same moment cannot see each other's effects. The rulebook says “in any order you choose”. Turn's default is “all at once”.
  • Optional replacements. Turn exceptions always fire. Rules like “you may … instead” need the decision asked in an earlier step.
  • No notion of an Action. “Once per Action” and “at the same time” have nothing to key on.
  • Silent timing mistakes. Several first attempts ran without errors but read state from the wrong moment.

Each of these has a concrete language change proposed in What to change.

67 special rules across 37 spirits.

Status means: works the rule was added without touching existing rules, and a run showed it doing what the text says. needs base hook it works, but only after changing an existing rule in core.t (the diff is shown). partial the core of the rule works and some clause is approximated or left out. not expressible the rule could not be written in Turn as it stands.

Reading Turn

Turn derives tuples that live on intervals of a partial order of moments. Episodes are tuples with a duration; a rule body reads left to right, matching tuples and asserting new ones, and by default the rest of the body runs inside what it matched. The full language is described in discussions/turn-tutorial.md (source). The code in this report uses an invented highlighting scheme that colors each sigil by what it does:

~launch an episode
~> >launch / match, then continue after it
+assert a fact (lasts to the end of time)
^assert inside the enclosing episode
? !ask a choice / constrain its options
{ => }exception: replace a tuple
/acc rule: body / computed row
#acc @sumdeclaration, aggregation
Landvariable
ravagerelation at the head of an atom
is gebuilt-in
-- p9comment (usually the rulebook sentence)

Every experiment is a set of .t files concatenated and run headless: run.sh core.t spirit-ocean.t. Player decisions are written as ?[rng] choices with a fixed seed, so a run is reproducible, and several seeds were tried where the choice mattered. All files are in si/ and reproduced in the appendix.

The base rules

The base slice (core.t) covers the Invader Phase (Ravage, Build, Explore), Blight with Presence destruction and cascades, Fear from destroyed Towns and Cities, Defend, the five-phase turn, Elements, Power speed, Push, adding Presence and Sacred Sites. Each rule carries the rulebook sentence it implements. Most read close to the text. Build is two rules, one per sentence:

Explore's “you only add one Explorer” falls out of a boolean acc relation, which holds each land at most once:

Blight's two consequences are two rules. The cascade reads has-blight at the start of add-blight, which is exactly “if the land already had Blight”:

Simultaneity was the first real bug

The natural reading of “the Invaders Ravage in each land of the shown type” launches one ravage episode per land. Turn makes those siblings: neither can see the other's effects. In a run, l2's Blight cascaded into l1 but could not see the Blight l1's own Ravage had just added, so l1 ended with two Blight and no second cascade, which no real play order allows. The rulebook says Powers resolve “in whatever order the players want”; Ravage needs the same. The fix is a loop that picks the next land:

It works, but it is boilerplate for a very common rulebook idiom (“for each X, in an order you choose”), and the +ravaged marker would leak into the next turn unless keyed by turn.

First extensions

Seven rules from expansions, Fear Cards, Power Cards and an Adversary were each written as a separate file and concatenated onto the unchanged base. Six worked; all six also ran together.

RuleSourceStatusHow
DiseaseBranch & Clawworksone exception: { build L => ~remove-one L disease }
WildsBranch & Clawworksone exception on explore
StrifeBranch & Clawworksexception on one Invader's damage contribution
Heavy MiningSweden, level 1workstrigger, plus two exceptions for “does not destroy Presence or cause cascades”
Words of WarningThunderspeaker cardworksexception reroutes fight-back to a start-of-Ravage snapshot
Avoid the DahanFear Card, level 1worksone exception on explore
BadlandsJagged Earthloopsthe boosted damage is caught again by the same exception

“When Invaders would X, instead Y” is exactly what exceptions are for. Disease is the rulebook sentence and one line:

Heavy Mining carries its own exception to the Blight rules, and the Turn version has the same shape as the English:

Words of Warning changes the order of Ravage (“Dahan deal damage simultaneously with Invaders”). It still went in as an addition, because the base names the fight-back step as its own episode that an exception can reroute:

Badlands failed. “+1 Damage per Badlands” re-emits damage-dahan with a bigger number, and the exception catches its own output forever:

The fix is in the base: write Damage to Dahan as summed contributions, so Badlands only adds one. Strife works for that reason: the base writes each Invader's damage as its own tuple and sums them. Extensibility depends on the base exposing each quantity the rulebook names.

The game itself is not purely additive either. Jagged Earth's Ravage Timing box says “This a change from existing rules” and reorders Ravage (JE p. 7).

Extension patterns

Across the extensions and all the spirits, an addition hooks into the base in a small number of ways. Each one only works where the base reads the thing through a relation the addition can extend.

Trigger 21 rules

“After X, do Y.” A rule matches the base episode for X and launches Y. Needs X to be its own episode, carrying who caused it.

Vengeance as a Burning Plague: Lingering Pestilence

Add rows 16 rules

Widen a set or add to a total. Needs the base to read through a relation, never inline.

Vital Strength of the Earth: Earth's Vitality

Devouring Teeth Lurk Underfoot: Territorial Aggression

Exception 13 rules

“When X would happen, instead Y.” Needs X to be a tuple emitted inside a context the rule can name.

Fathomless Mud of the Swamp: Offer No Firm Foundations

Counts as 6 rules

“Your Presence in Wetlands counts as a Sacred Site.” Rows added to a view the base reads everything through.

River Surges in Sunlight: River's Domain

New state 5 rules

A new resource or location. Time on Fractured Days' panel is Presence at a location, counted by a sum.

Fractured Days Split the Sky: Fragments of Shattered Time

Narrow a choice 4 rules

An extra ! on a named choice. Constraints are conjunctive, so they can only remove options.

Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island: Deep Slumber

Two shapes have a second, less obvious requirement. A scoped exception (Heavy Mining, Stone's Bedrock, Towering Roots' Vitality) works only if the base runs the consequences of an event inside that event's episode, as add-blight does with its Presence destruction and cascade. A late override (Swiftness of Lightning) works only if the quantity is a latest-value-wins relation (@last), so “as if it were Fast” is just a later value.

All spirits

Each spirit below quotes its special rules as printed (icons shown as labels), gives the status and mechanism, the key Turn lines with a link to their place in the source, what the run showed, and notes. Chips in the table jump to the rule.

The forks that wrote the spirits also had to add rulebook machinery that the base slice lacks: Energy, Damage and Health, Range and targeting, Growth, Events, presence tracks, and Time Passes. That work is marked BASE-EXT in each file. It is additive, but it was written several times under different names, so the spirit files run one at a time against core.t and do not yet all load together. Merging those into one shared library is the obvious next step.

Lightning's Swift Strike

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-lightning.t

SWIFTNESS OF LIGHTNING

worksoverride (@last)
For every Air you have, you may use 1 Slow Power as if it were Fast. (Power Cards or your Innate Powers.)

Run: seeds 7/3/11 with 2 Air and 3 Slow cards: exactly two cards get made-fast and use-power in the Fast phase; the third resolves in the Slow phase; no card resolves twice

Speed is an @last acc, so "as if it were Fast" is a later contribution and the base Slow phase skips the card on its own (One Use!). The Air count is re-read on every use, as the FAQ requires. First attempt made the same card Fast twice: the continuation ran inside swift-choice, before made-fast existed; `fast-phase, >swift-choice` fixed it. Innate Powers are not modeled. Port to fresh-left `^` (v2-caret-fresh-left): `^made-fast` from a separate `turn` rule started at a moment incomparable with the next `swiftness`, so the count never saw it; `made-fast` is now asserted in the chain that uses the Power and asks again, and names its turn so the speed override lasts exactly that turn.

  • A rule's continuation runs inside the episode it first matched, so reads there cannot see facts that start when that episode ends; nothing warns about it (fix: `parent, >ep, ...`).

River Surges in Sunlight

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-river.t

RIVER'S DOMAIN

workscounts-as view
Your Presence in Wetlands counts as Sacred Site.

Run: ss-report river l2 (a single Presence p1 in wetland l2 is a Sacred Site); the lone Presence in mountain l3 is not

One acc row added to the base sacred-site view. Reading terrain through terrain-for power means an Ocean made a Coastal Wetland by Ocean's Hungry Grasp would also count -- an interaction neither rule mentions, which falls out of routing every terrain read through the view. Only works because the base computes sacred-site as a view (not inline `presence-count S L N, ge N 2` in each consumer).

Shadows Flicker Like Flame

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-shadows.t

SHADOWS OF THE DAHAN

worksadd-rows (widen)
Whenever you use a Power, you may pay 1 Energy to target a land with Dahan regardless of the Power's Range. (Power Cards or your Innate Powers.)

Run: target-dest rows: shadows mantle l3 0 (range 0), l1 1, l2 1 (lands with Dahan); 6 seeds targeted l1/l2 and energy-report shadows 0 after paying; with 0 Energy only `target-dest shadows mantle l3 0` exists

Needed a BASE-EXT targeting step whose choice ranges over target-dest S P L Cost: the cost column is what lets a widening rule also attach a price ('you may pay 1 Energy to ...'). Without the cost column the payment would need negation ('pay only if the land was not already in range'). rng sometimes picks the paid option even when the land is also in range for free (both rows exist); a human would not -- harmless for 'may pay'.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Energy (#acc energy @sum of energy-change contributions); Range (#acc within land land nat, Peano, bounded by range-value facts); Targeting (targeting S P episode: joint choice ?L C over target-dest S P L Cost, pay Cost, ^target S P L); use-power triggers targeting for power:targets-land.

  • No negative-number literal arithmetic: paying K Energy needs `minus 0 K NK` then a contribution of NK (a #js-def), since @sum is the only accumulator.
  • Range comparison over Peano needs a bounded recursive acc (`within`); numeric ranges would need a numeric BFS in JS.

Vital Strength of the Earth

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-earth.t

EARTH'S VITALITY

worksadd-rows (widen)
Defend 3 in every land where you have Sacred Site.

Run: without the rule: damage-land l2 5; with Earth's Sacred Site in l2: damage-land l2 2 (5 - Defend 3)

A static ability is a standing acc contribution to the base defend-total @sum, recomputed every moment, so it switches off automatically when the Sacred Site is lost (e.g. Blight destroys a Presence). Simplest rule in the group: one line.

A Spread of Rampant Green

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-green.t · core-green.t

CHOKE THE LAND WITH GREEN

worksexception (instead)
Whenever Invaders would Ravage or Build in a land with your Sacred Site, you may prevent it by destroying one of your Presence in that land.

Run: seeds 3,6 answer yes: `_ravage_prime1 l2; choke l2; move g1 destroyed`, no `ravage l2`, l2 Blight stays 1; answer no: `ravage l2; damage-land l2 5`. Build: seed 1 yes on l2 -> `choke l2`, `build l1` still happens

An exception cannot be optional: once installed it always replaces, and a declined replacement cannot re-emit `ravage L` (it would be intercepted again and loop). So the 'may' is asked first (when the base chooses the land to Ravage -- ravage-chosen -- and at the start of the Build step), and only a 'yes' installs the exception. For Build the base has no build-target view, so its card/terrain/invaders condition is restated in the spirit file.

STEADY REGENERATION

needs base hookadd-rows (widen)
When adding Presence to the board via Growth, you may optionally use your destroyed Presence. If the island is Healthy, do so freely. If the island is Blighted, doing so costs 1 Energy per destroyed Presence you add.

Run: seed 5: `move g3 l3` -- the destroyed Presence g3 was added by Growth; other seeds chose g4 from the supply

core.t hard-codes `presence-of S P, at P supply` as the source of an added Presence (and, as written, moves EVERY supply Presence -- a core bug). core-green.t makes the source a choice over a presence-source view; then the rule is two added rows (Healthy: free; Blighted: offered only with Energy >= 1) plus a trigger that charges 1 Energy. 'via Growth' is checked by requiring the growth S episode to be alive in the acc body. The Blighted Island flip is not modeled (island-state is a fact).

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Energy (#acc energy); Growth reduced to `growth S, ~add-presence S`; island-state healthy fact (no Blight Card).

Change to core.t
--- core.t	2026-10-09 12:33:29.216961840 -0700
+++ core-green.t	2026-10-09 13:11:31.589939037 -0700
@@ -250,8 +250,15 @@
   ?[rng] L
   !(presence-dest S L)
   ~presence-choice S L
-presence-choice S L, is L X, presence-of S P, at P supply, ~>placing S P, ~move P X
-placing S P, ^nothing
+-- which Presence is added is also a choice, over presence-source (by
+-- default: the Presence still in the supply, i.e. on the tracks)
+#acc presence-source : spirit e
+presence-of S P, at P supply / presence-source S P
+presence-choice S L, is L X
+  ?[rng] P
+  !(presence-source S P)
+  ~placing S P X
+placing S C X, is C P, ~move P X
 
 -- Beasts are counted through a view, so other pieces can "count as" Beasts.
 #acc beasts-at : e land
  • Exceptions are unconditional: 'you may prevent it' must be decided by a choice placed before the intercepted tuple is emitted; deciding inside the replacement cannot fall back to the original (re-emission is re-intercepted).
  • A choice domain derived from an acc that depends on the choice's own follow-up episode is silently empty (my first yes-no acc keyed on choke-ask): the choice resolves to nothing with no warning.

Thunderspeaker

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-thunderspeaker.t

ALLY OF THE DAHAN

partialtrigger (after/when)
Your Presence may move with Dahan. (Whenever a Dahan moves from 1 of your lands to another land, you may move 1 Presence along with it.)

Run: seed 2: two Dahan pushed out of l2; ally-choice moved t2 with one of them (`move t2 l3`). seed 3: t2 moved with BOTH Dahan (`move t2 l3; move t2 l1`)

The trigger is easy (match the base move episode; `at D From` read at its start is where the Dahan came from). Wrong when two Dahan move at the same moment (one Push of several Dahan = sibling push-to episodes): each trigger sees the same Presence still in the origin and both may take it. Correct only if the base moves pieces one at a time.

SWORN TO VICTORY

workstrigger (after/when)
After a Ravage Action destroys 1 or more Dahan, for each Dahan Destroyed, Destroy 1 of your Presence within 1 Range. 1 2

Run: l2 Ravage destroys 2 Dahan -> `sworn thunder l2 2; ... 1; ... 0` destroying 2 distinct Presence within 1 (all 6 seeds, no duplicate destroys); l1 loses 1 Dahan -> sworn l1 1 with no Presence left -> no-op

Two fixes were needed: (1) 'for each Dahan destroyed, destroy 1 Presence' as independent per-Dahan firings ran at one moment and could pick the same Presence -> rewritten as a counted loop; (2) placing it 'after the Ravage' (`ravage-step, >ravage L`) made it concurrent with the next land's Ravage (whose Blight destroyed the same Presence) -> anchored `ravage L, >dahan-fight-back L` instead, i.e. after the last step but inside the Ravage. That depends on knowing the base's last sub-step. dahan-lost is keyed by land only (+ facts), so a multi-turn game would accumulate counts across turns.

  • 'For each X, do Y (choosing)' as parallel firings lets choices at the same moment collide; needs a sequential counted loop (or a builtin 'for each, one at a time').
  • 'After episode E' via `parent, >E` runs concurrently with whatever the base starts after E; to run strictly before the next base step one must hook inside E after its known last sub-step (`E, >last-step`) -- there is no 'at the end of E, still inside E' form.
  • Simultaneous moves (one Push of several pieces) are sibling episodes, so per-move triggers can't see each other's effects (Ally of the Dahan moved one Presence twice).

Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-bringer.t

TO DREAM A THOUSAND DEATHS

partialexception (instead)
Your Powers never cause Damage, nor can they Destroy anything other than your own Presence. When your Powers would Destroy (or deal enough Damage to Destroy) Explorer / Town / City, instead generate 0/2/5 Fear. The Power Pushes all Explorer / Town it would Destroy. Notes: A single Power cannot Destroy a given Invader more than once. Powers that cause Damage via Dahan are affected just like all others. All effects other than Damage/Destroy work as usual.

Run: with the rule: Town -> `fear-from *63 2`, `push bringer *63 l1`; Explorer dealt 1 Damage -> `fear-from *100 0`, pushed; Dahan -> dream-destroy only (not destroyed); total fear 2. Control without the rule: all three destroyed, fear 1

Maps very directly: two exceptions scoped to this Spirit's use-power episode replace destroy / damage-piece; 'or deal enough Damage to Destroy' falls out of checking Health inside the replacement. Own-Presence destruction is untouched because the base routes it through destroy-presence, not destroy. Missing: accumulated Damage across instructions (BASE-EXT is single-hit), 'a single Power cannot Destroy a given Invader more than once', Damage dealt by Dahan a Power moves (only matters once Powers can make Dahan deal Damage). The exception RHS may not mention the Spirit, so the push looks the Bringer up by its special-rule fact (would be ambiguous with two Bringers).

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Health (kind:health facts) and `damage-piece X N` that destroys when N >= Health (single-hit, no accumulated Damage).

  • Exception RHS may only use the intercepted tuple's variables, so context (which Spirit's Power) must be re-derived in a helper rule; with two copies of a Spirit this would be ambiguous.

Ocean's Hungry Grasp

Base · wiki · archived copy · spirit-ocean.t

OCEAN IN PLAY

workscounts-as view
You may add/move Presence into Oceans, but may not add/move Presence into Inland lands. On boards where you have 1 or more Presence, Oceans are treated as Coastal Wetlands for Spirit Powers and Blight. You Drown any Invaders or Dahan moved to those Oceans.

Run: Presence added into `sea` (never Inland l2/l3); push-dest offers `sea`; a pushed Town that lands in `sea` is drowned (drown *85, fear 1)

Each clause is one mechanism: widen the Presence choice (acc rows), narrow it (extra `!`), counts-as land per context (land-for power/blight), and a trigger on move. Needed core.t to read lands through land-for <context>, with one base line changed (cascade reads land-for blight). The FAQ says Fear/Event pushes cannot drown; push-dest is keyed by spirit, not by cause, so this is not modeled. First attempt never drowned: the `+human` facts were top-level and could not join the move episode.

DROWNING

partialtrigger (after/when)
Destroy Drowned pieces, placing Drowned Invaders here. At any time you may exchange (X) Health of these Invaders for 1 Energy, where X = number of players. (Ignore modifiers to Invader Health.)

Run: drown *85; move *85 ocean-mat; fear 1 (destroying a Town still generates Fear, as the FAQ confirms)

"At any time you may exchange (X) Health ... for 1 Energy" is not modeled: Turn has no "at any time" construct, so the option would have to be offered at every choice point.

  • Top-level `+` facts sit on a branch unordered with the game and silently never join with episodes inside it; they must live in setup.
  • No way to express an option available "at any time".

Keeper of the Forbidden Wilds

Branch & Claw · wiki · archived copy · spirit-keeper.t

FORBIDDEN GROUND

workstrigger (after/when)
After you create a Sacred Site, Push all Dahan from that land.

Run: sacred-site-created keeper l3 k2; forbidden-ground keeper l3 (once); push keeper *127 l3 -> l2

'After you create a Sacred Site' is a transition: the move that finds presence-count S L = 1 at its start creates it. The trigger needed a generic per-phase window (BASE-EXT `^phase`) plus a phase-scoped tag so it fires exactly once and is ordered before the next phase. Port to fresh-left `^`: the generic `^phase` window starts at its own moment inside each phase, incomparable with the move, so the trigger never fired; it is now one rule per phase, anchored on the phase episode and continuing after the move (`>move P L`).

FORBIDDEN GROUND (Dahan Events)

worksadd-constraint (narrow)
Dahan Events never move Dahan to your Sacred Site, but Powers can do so.

Run: Event pushes 3 Dahan out of l2 (adjacent l1, l3=Sacred Site): all 3 go to l1 in every seed

Narrows only the Event's push choice (named by push-to), so Powers are unaffected. Needed a 'not a Sacred Site' relation: done by adding a 0 row to presence-count (additive) and `lt N 2`, since acc has no negation. Events are modeled as the pusher `event`.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: presence-count 0 rows; not-sacred-site; Event as a push actor; the trigger written once per phase (spirit/fast/invader/slow-phase).

  • `turn, >move P L` floats: it is after the move but unordered relative to the following phases, so effects can be invisible to the next phase; anchor triggers on a per-phase window instead.
  • `phase, >move P L` alone fires once per later phase (>p only requires p to end before the window ends); restricting to the phase the move happened in needed a phase-scoped tag: `phase, (move P L), ..., ^tag` then `phase, tag, >move P L`.
  • A head variable that is not bound in the body (I dropped S from the second rule) silently becomes a fresh object instead of an error (`forbidden-ground *8671 l3`).
  • 'Not a Sacred Site' needs a complement; with no acc negation it is `presence-count S L N, lt N 2` plus explicit 0 rows.

Sharp Fangs Behind the Leaves

Branch & Claw · wiki · archived copy · spirit-fangs.t

ALLY OF THE BEASTS

workstrigger (after/when)
Your Presence may move with Beasts. (Whenever a Beasts moves from 1 of your lands to another land, you may move 1 Presence along with it.)

Run: push fangs *171 l3 -> l2; ally-choice picks f1 (seeds 2,4) or f2 (seed 3): move f1 l2; or declines (seeds 7,1)

A trigger on the base `move` episode: `at`/`beasts-at` are read at the move's start, which is exactly 'moves from 1 of your lands'. First attempt read the destination after the move and got the old location; From/To must be passed along from the move itself. Two Beasts moving in parallel can both offer the same Presence (sibling concurrency).

CALL FORTH PREDATORS

worksnew state
During each Spirit Phase, you may replace 1 of your Presence with 1 Beasts. The replaced Presence leaves the game. (It was not destroyed, so things which return destroyed Presence cannot bring it back.)

Run: seeds 7,1: move f1 out-of-game; add-piece l3 beasts (new Beasts *7038 then pushed too)

'Leaves the game' is a location distinct from `destroyed`, so effects that return destroyed Presence naturally cannot find it.

  • Reading a location 'after' a move from a sibling rule sees the pre-move value (the sibling is unordered with the moved fact); pass values from the triggering episode's arguments instead.
  • 'You may' needs an explicit `decline` option row in the choice domain each time.

Heart of the Wildfire

Promo Pack 1 · wiki · archived copy · spirit-wildfire.t

BLAZING PRESENCE

partialtrigger (after/when)
Post-Setup, after your Presence is added/moved, in the land it goes to: For each Fire showing on your Presence Tracks, do 1 Damage. If 2 Fire or more are showing on your Presence Tracks, add 1 Blight. Push all Beasts and any number of Dahan. If you add multiple Presence into a land at the same time, only do the above effects once.

Run: move w2 l3; blaze wildfire l3; deal-damage l3 2 -> destroy Explorer; add-blight l3; push wildfire Beasts l3 -> l2; per-Dahan push/stay choice

Four sentences map to four rules on the `blaze` episode. Needed BASE-EXT Damage/Health (point-by-point damage with per-piece @sum damage) and a 'Fire showing on tracks' fact. Not modeled: 'If you add multiple Presence into a land at the same time, only do the above effects once' -- each Presence move triggers separately; deduping needs an 'Action' identity Turn doesn't expose. Port to fresh-left ^ / #acc (2026-10-12): the trigger is anchored on each phase episode (one rule per phase; the snippet shows the Spirit phase) instead of a generic `^phase` window, which no longer overlaps the moves in the phase. Anchoring on `turn` instead was tried and is wrong: the blaze then runs concurrently with the later phases, so its Blight is invisible to them.

DESTRUCTIVE NATURE

worksexception (instead)

Exceptions whose contexts are the Spirit-effect episodes (blaze, use-power) drop `move X destroyed` for this Spirit's Presence; cascades are nested inside the add-blight that caused them, so '(This includes cascades.)' is free. The contexts must be enumerated (Powers, special rules...); 'Spirit effect' is not a first-class notion.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Invader Health; per-piece damage (@sum of +hit facts) and a point-by-point deal-damage loop with destroy at Health; track-fire fact; per-phase triggers anchored on each phase episode.

  • 'At the same time' (one Action adding several Presence) has no handle: Turn has no notion of Action identity to dedupe triggers on.

worksadd-rows (widen)
Some of your Actions let you Prepare Element Markers, which are kept here until used. Choose the Elements freely. (I.e., you are not limited to Elements you have at the time.) Each Element Marker spent grants 1 of that Element for a single Action. (E.g., one Power use.)

Markers are pieces on Memory's mat; spending adds rows to the base `elements` @sum that live only while the Action does ('for a single Action'). The grant had to be scoped with `action S A, >spend-marker ..., ^spent-on` -- a plain ^ inside the spend episode vanished before the Action read it. Port to fresh-left `^`: `action S A, >spend-marker ..., ^spent-on` now starts `spent-on` at a moment incomparable with the Action's later steps, so the grant was missing "during"; `spent-on` is now a fact asserted when the marker is spent, and the acc rule's `action S A` alone scopes the grant to the Action.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Power Card locations (hand/discard/forgotten via `at`), forget/discard verbs, in-hand view; an `action` episode wrapping a Power use.

  • `^x` emitted in a short sub-episode lives only there; effects meant for 'the rest of the Action' need `action, >sub, ^x`.

Adjacency in core is a plain fact relation, so a Spirit can widen it just by emitting more adjacent tuples with a bounded interval; every acc/choice that reads adjacent picks them up. Partial: the way is chosen once at the start of the Fast phase and lasts the turn. 'change which lands are adjacent once between Actions' needs an adjacency to stop holding at an arbitrary later moment, i.e. retraction; Turn tuples only end with their enclosing episode, so a way would have to be an episode that the next change closes — no construct for that. Also no 'it persists across turns until changed'.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Energy as `#acc energy : spirit @sum` over energy-change facts; a Power Card 'Destroy 1 <kind>' in its target land.

  • State kept in an episode vanishes when the episode ends (I first wrote `~energy-change finder 1`; the acc lost it); persistent resources must be `+` facts, and per-turn ones need `turn, >…, ^`.
  • No retraction / 'until changed': a fact holds to top and a ^ tuple ends with its scope, so a toggleable state (Open the Ways) can only be approximated per turn; an @last relation can model 'current value' but not a set of tuples that other rules match directly (adjacent).
  • Symbol inequality still needs a #js-def (neq) for 'two different lands'.

Run: power-damage teeth gnaw l3 2 (printed 1); 'assign-damage l3 2; count l3 town 0; fear 1'. Control: 'assign-damage l3 1; count l3 town 1; fear 0'.

Exactly the 'reify every modifiable quantity as a @sum' pattern: once the base sums a Power's Damage per use, '+1 Damage total for the Power, even if it damages multiple Invaders' is one contribution, and 'Damage-Dealing Powers' is the guard power:damage P N, gt N 0. Uses bx-damage.t.

worksexception (instead)

partialadd-rows (widen)
At your Sacred Site, Invaders have -1 Health (min. 1).

Health is a @sum relation (bx-damage.t), so -1 is one added contribution. 'min. 1' is approximated by only applying -1 to Invaders whose printed Health is above 1; that is exact only while this is the sole Health modifier — a clamp over the sum is not additive and would need the base to expose effective-health = max(1, raw sum) as a second layer. Partial because the shared Damage model has no partial Damage carry-over.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: bx-damage.t (shared with teeth): Invader Health as `#acc health : e @sum` from kind:health; a Power's Damage as `#acc power-damage : spirit power land @sum`; Damage assignment by repeated rng choice of an Invader whose Health fits the remaining Damage (no partial Damage). Run: run.sh core.t bx-damage.t spirit-heat.t

  • Recursive episodes nest (assign-damage inside assign inside assign-damage), so an outer episode is still alive during the inner step and an acc relation keyed only by land (assignable L V) mixed rows from D=2 and D=1; fix: key the acc row by every argument of the episode (assignable L D V).

Nature Incarnate · wiki · archived copy · spirit-behemoth.t

worksnew state
You have an Incarna ( Ember-Eyed Behemoth). Once per turn, during the Spirit, Fast, or Slow phase, you may either: Push Ember-Eyed Behemoth ; or Add or Move Ember-Eyed Behemoth to any of your Sacred Site on the island.

'Once per turn' = a use counter (@sum with a 0 row for 'unused') compared with an allowance (@sum, so Strides can add 1). The offer happens in each of the three phases with a decline option. Uses are recorded with + inside the choice episode; in a multi-turn game they would need a turn key (no 'until end of turn' fact that is also visible to later reads without floating).

worksadd-rows (widen) + exception (instead)
On any turn that you don't use Innate Powers, you may use The Behemoth Rises an additional time. (When you use an Innate Power, cover this Special Rule with a Reminder Marker; when you use this Special Rule, cover your Innate Power.)

Run: Seeds 1,3,5,6: two uses, Innate not used; seeds 2,4,8: one use, use-power behemoth smash; seed 7: no use, Innate used. Never two uses plus the Innate.

The physical 'cover' markers are a mutual exclusion; Turn expresses it as a conditional extra allowance row (no Innate used yet) plus an exception that drops the Innate's use-power once 2 uses happened. Concurrency caveat: a Slow-phase offer and the Slow Innate start at the same moment, so both read 'unused'.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Innate Powers modeled as played powers with power:innate; Incarna as a presence-of row and incarna-of fact; push reused from core.

Nature Incarnate · wiki · archived copy · spirit-hearth.t · core-hearth.t

needs base hookexception (instead)
Blight added in your lands does not Destroy your Presence if Dahan are present. (Ravage Actions Destroy Dahan before added Blight destroys Presence and cascades.)

Run: core-hearth.t: with Dahan alive only River's p1 is destroyed (move p1 destroyed), all Hearth Presence survive; without Fortify, Dahan die first (kill-dahan l1 1) and then move h1 destroyed. Against unmodified core.t, h1 survives in l1 although its Dahan was killed: kill-dahan and add-blight are concurrent siblings there.

The rule's parenthetical fixes an order the base leaves concurrent: core Ravage launches damage-land and damage-dahan as siblings, so the guard 'Dahan are present' read at add-blight start cannot see the Ravage's Dahan kills. core-hearth.t sequences damage-dahan before damage-land (one-line change). The exception filters on this spirit's own Presence by intercepting `move X destroyed` for X bound in the context (other spirits' Presence still destroyed).

needs base hookadd-rows (widen) + exception (instead)

Run: kill-dahan l1 0 and kill-dahan l2 0 with 3 and 5 Damage (Health 6); the Event's event-destroy fires but no Dahan in l2 is destroyed (3 Dahan in l2 at report). Without Fortify: event destroys *295 and Ravage kills Dahan.

core.t hard-coded 'every 2 Damage destroys one Dahan' (half D N); +4 Health needs Health as a summable quantity, so core-hearth.t adds `#acc dahan-health : land @sum` with base row 2 and divides by it; the spirit then adds a 4 row (pure addition). Health is per land, not per Dahan (fine while all Dahan in a land share the bonus). Events/Blight Cards don't exist in core; a minimal event-action episode was added as BASE-EXT. 'damage' and 'replace' by Events are not modeled (no per-piece damage or replace in core).

LOYAL GUARDIAN

partialtrigger (after/when)
When all Dahan leave one of your lands, your Presence may Move with those Dahan. (Each Dahan can Bring any number of Presence.)

Run: Slow-phase push of l1's only Dahan to l2: loyal-follow hearth l1 l2, loyal-answer h1 l2 ..., move h1 l2; report shows h1 in l2.

'All Dahan leave' is approximated as 'the last Dahan in the land moves' (read via land:count at the move's start). Several Dahan moved by one action (Gather/Push up to N) are not grouped, so 'each Dahan can bring Presence' to different destinations is only per-move. Needs neq (#js-def) to exclude moves within a land.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Event Actions as an `event-action E` episode (an event that destroys 1 Dahan in a land). core-hearth.t variant: Dahan Health as #acc dahan-health (@sum, base 2) and Ravage damaging Dahan before the land.

Change to core.t
--- core.t	2026-10-09 12:33:29.216961840 -0700
+++ core-hearth.t	2026-10-09 13:09:04.188397132 -0700
@@ -106,8 +106,8 @@
 invaders-deal-damage L
   ~>tally L
   invader-damage L Raw, defend-total L Def, minus Raw Def D0, pos D0 D
+  ~>damage-dahan L D
   ~damage-land L D
-  ~damage-dahan L D
 tally L, ^tallied
 
 -- "1. Invaders Damage the Land: If 2 or more Damage is dealt, add a Blight
@@ -115,7 +115,11 @@
 damage-land L D, ge D 2, ~add-blight L
 
 -- "2. Invaders Fight the Dahan: Every 2 points of Damage destroys one Dahan."
-damage-dahan L D, half D N, ~kill-dahan L N
+#js-def div +A +B -C { yield [Math.floor(A / B)] }
+-- p16 "Each Dahan has 2 Health" (Health exposed as a summable quantity)
+#acc dahan-health : land @sum
+land L / dahan-health L 2
+damage-dahan L D, dahan-health L H, div D H N, ~kill-dahan L N
 kill-dahan L N, gt N 0, land:count L dahan C, gt C 0
   ?[rng] V
   !(at V L, piece:kind V dahan)
  • Sibling sub-episodes launched with plain `~a, ~b` from one rule body are concurrent, so a guard in b-triggered rules cannot see a's effects; ordering must be written into the base with `~>` (here: damage-dahan before damage-land).
  • Hard-coded arithmetic in base rules (half D N) blocks additive modifiers; quantities like Health must be @sum relations from the start.
  • Exceptions cannot filter on 'whose' a choice-based destroy is (destroy-presence carries an opaque choice term), so the exception intercepts the downstream `move X destroyed` with X bound in the context instead.
  • 'When all X leave' needs grouping by action; Turn has no notion of an action boundary to aggregate moves over, so the trigger is per-move.

worksexception (instead)
Some of your Actions Add Vitality Tokens ( Vitality). (Each Vitality in a land with no Blight prevents 1 Blight from being added, then is Removed.)

Run: add-blight l1; remove-token l1 vitality; count l1 vitality 2, count l1 blight 0 (3 Vitality, Ravage of 3 Damage).

Same shape as Sweden's Heavy Mining: the context is the add-blight episode itself, so the guard (Vitality present, no Blight) is read at the right moment, and the Blight piece plus the Presence destruction it causes are replaced. Cascade needs no exception (a land without Blight never cascades). Two concurrent add-blights in one land would both see the same Vitality.

HEART-TREE GUARDS THE LAND

partialadd-rows (widen) + exception (instead) + trigger (after/when)
You have an Incarna ( Towering Roots of the Jungle). Your Powers get +1 Range if Towering Roots of the Jungle is in the origin land. Invaders/ Dahan / Beasts can't be damaged or destroyed at Towering Roots of the Jungle. Empower Towering Roots of the Jungle the first time it's in a land with 3 or more Vitality. Skip all Build Actions at empowered Towering Roots of the Jungle.

Run: could-target roots grow l1/l2/l3 for a range-0 Power: l2 is reachable only from the Incarna's land with the +1; empowered tree after 3 Vitality; l1 Ravage destroys nothing (count l1 dahan 1, town 1, explorer 1); only `build l2` occurs, build l1 skipped.

Range bonus is a pure @sum contribution once the base computes targets from range-bonus. Protection is only for destruction during Ravage: an exception guard is evaluated when its context starts, and there is no interval-valued 'Incarna is in L' tuple to use as a context (location is a per-moment @last acc row), so 'at the Incarna' cannot be a standing guard for all destroy sources. Empowerment needs a check inside every event that can make it true (Incarna moves, Vitality added) - acc views cannot emit. Incarna is modeled as an extra presence-of row (counts as Presence), so Blight can destroy it.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Range/land targeting (bounded reach acc, range-bonus @sum, power-target domain, targeting/target-chosen/targeted episodes); remove-token; Incarna as a presence-of row.

  • No interval-valued state: 'while the Incarna is in L' cannot be an exception context, because location is an acc @last value (per-moment rows), not a tuple with an interval; guards are read once at context start.
  • Acc relations cannot trigger emissions, so 'the first time condition C becomes true' must be re-checked inside every episode that can change C.
  • A trigger anchored on a wide window (`game, >add-piece ... , +empowered I`) placed +empowered at a moment not ordered before the later build-step, so the Build-skip guard never saw it; anchoring the check inside the add-piece episode (`add-piece L vitality, >move V L, ...`) fixed it. Silent failure.
  • JS relations work inside acc bodies (used for bounded reach with plus/lt).

You have an Incarna ( Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine). Empower Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine after uncovering Empowered. You may Abduct 1 Explorer / Town at empowered Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine each Fast phase. To Abduct a piece, Move it to The Endless Dark ( Endless Dark). Presence tracks are not modeled: 'uncovering' is an `uncover S empowered-space` episode. 'Alone' is checked at the start of the Power, not of the destroy instruction. Damage is not modeled (destroy only). The 'you lose' clause needs a count of destinations (@sum with a 0 row) because an empty choice silently resolves to nothing. First version wrongly applied 'instead Abduct' inside the Endless Dark: the invader count had rows for it; guarding with `land L` fixed it.

worksadd-rows (widen)
Your land-targeting Powers can target Endless Dark as if it were a land, ignoring Range. ( Endless Dark is Inland and has no terrain.)

Run: targeted breath dread endless-dark in several seeds; an Explorer there is destroyed normally by the Power.

One added row to the target domain. 'Inland, no terrain' holds automatically: no land:terrain row and no ocean adjacency.

A SPACE OF STRANGE AND INFINITE DARKNESS / TRAPPED IN THE ENDLESS DARK

partialcounts-as view
The Endless Dark ( Endless Dark) is on the island, but isn't a land and isn't on any board. This can't be a Sacred Site. Spirits can't target this even if they have Presence here. Adding Blight here doesn't destroy Presence. Special rules that affect lands do nothing here. Invaders can't take Actions here. Pieces here are on the island when checking for Victory/Defeat. / Fear Cards and Token Events affect pieces here as if this were an Inland land, but can't remove Invaders here - when ttruncated

Run: invader-on-island rows include pieces in endless-dark; no Ravage/Build/Explore there; untested for Fear Cards (none in core).

Most clauses hold for free because endless-dark has no `land` row and every base rule quantifies over land (closed-world default). Only the positive 'counts as' clauses need rows (on-island, land-for fear). The truncated remainder of Trapped (removal -> escape?) is not formalized.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Range/land targeting (as in spirit-roots.t), land:invader-count, test-only target narrowing, Incarna as a presence-of row.

  • A choice with no options resolves to nothing silently, so 'if there is no legal destination, you lose' needs a separate @sum count of options with a 0 row.
  • Helper views that range over all locations (land:invader-count via `at X L`) leak into non-lands; every rule about lands needs an explicit `land L` guard. Closed-world 'not a land' is otherwise a strength: most Endless Dark restrictions needed no rules.
  • A test can narrow a rng choice with an extra `!` constraint read through the named choice tuple (`targeting S dread, (target-chosen S dread T), !(test-target T)`), which is a handy way to force scenarios.

Relentless Gaze of the Sun

Nature Incarnate · wiki · archived copy · spirit-gaze.t

RELENTLESS PUNISHMENT

workstrigger (after/when)
After using a Power Card, if you had at least 3 Presence in the origin land, you may Repeat it any number of times on the same target land(s) (ignoring origin, Range, and target requirements) by paying both: the Energy cost of the Power, and 1 Energy per previous use of the Power this turn each time you Repeat the Power. (You may Repeat each Power Card multiple times, but its 1st Repeat costs 1 extra, its 2nd Repeat costs 2 extra, etc. Check if the origin has at least 3 Presence when you target it the first time.)

Run: 6 Energy, cost-1 card, 3 Presence at origin: seeds 2/3: relentless-ask gaze scorch 1 2 -> energy-spend gaze 2 -> resolved-again gaze scorch l2 -> relentless-ask gaze scorch 2 3 -> energy-spend gaze 3 -> resolved-again ...; gaze-energy 1 (next Repeat would cost 4, not offered). Seeds 7/1 decline the 2nd Repeat (gaze-energy 4).

Pure trigger after `use-power`, plus a self-recursive Repeat loop whose argument U counts previous uses. The origin check happens once, at the first use, matching the parenthetical. Approximations: '1 Energy per previous use of the Power this turn' is tracked by the loop counter, so uses from other Repeat effects aren't counted; origin/target are scenario facts (no targeting/Range model); the trigger is written against `turn, >use-power` rather than the current phase, so Repeats are not confined to the phase they started in.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Energy as an @sum acc of energy-gain / energy-spend facts (negative contributions via a `neg` #js-def), `plus` #js-def, power:cost / power:card / power:origin / power:target facts, a yes/no `may` domain.

  • Arithmetic on costs (cost + previous uses) and spending needs #js-def plus/neg; Energy is an @sum with negative contributions.
  • No per-phase 'after' anchor: `turn, >use-power ...` continues until end of turn, so to confine Repeats to the current phase you'd need one rule per phase (no variable over episode names).

Wounded Waters Bleeding

Nature Incarnate · wiki · archived copy · spirit-wounded.t

SEEKING A PATH TOWARDS HEALING

workstrigger (after/when)
After playing cards each Spirit Phase: Claim a Healing Marker (Element Marker) matching whichever of Water or Animal you have more of. ( You break ties.) You may then Claim a Healing Card if you meet its requirements. ( You can claim your first Healing Card on Turn 3.) Then Destroy 1 Presence or Forget a Power Card ( unless a Healing Card just removed this rule).

Run: 3 turns, seed 7: seeking-on-turn 0, healing-marker wounded water, paid-cost 0 w1; seeking-on-turn 1, healing-marker wounded animal, paid-cost 1 tide; seeking-on-turn 2, healing-marker wounded water, claimed wounded serene-waters (no cost paid). Seed 2 declines the card on turn 3 and pays (paid-cost 2 w3). A 4-turn run has no seeking on turn 4 after the claim (rule removed).

The three steps are a sequenced episode (`seeking S` -> claim-marker; maybe-claim-healing; pay-the-cost). The tie-break is a choice between Water and Animal. 'Unless a Healing Card just removed this rule' is a scoped exception on pay-the-cost; removing the rule for later turns is a fact plus an exception on `seeking`. The Healing Card (serene-waters: 2 Water markers, removes the rule) is INVENTED, since the real Healing Cards weren't in the sources; the real cards' replacement rules are not modeled. Bugs hit along the way: `spirit-phase, >play-cards` re-fired for every previous turn, and `+rule-removed` asserted from a rule anchored on a forever-fact wasn't visible on the next turn.

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Multiple turns (each finished turn starts the next, counted by a `turns-done` @sum acc), a play-cards / after-play-cards step in the Spirit Phase, Power Cards with a location (hand/forgotten) and `forget`, a yes/no `may` domain. The played cards are a turn-scoped acc view (`#acc played`, `turn … / played …`): a `turn, ^played …` view now starts concurrently with the phases.

  • `>p` matches ANY earlier p, including previous turns' episodes (`spirit-phase, >play-cards` fired once per earlier turn); workaround: an explicit `after-...` step, or key the episode by turn number (`>healing-ask S H R N` with `turns-done N`).
  • A fact asserted by a rule anchored on another forever-fact (`claimed S H, ..., +rule-removed ...`) floats and wasn't visible to the next turn's exception; assert it inside a bounded episode (the seeking step) instead.
  • core is single-turn; multi-turn needs a counter and a `game, >turn, ... ~turn` rule. core's `+ravaged X -> 1` (#agg, to top) then leaks, so turns 2+ never Ravage.

Dances Up Earthquakes

Nature Incarnate · wiki · archived copy · spirit-dances.t

BEGIN A DANCE OF DECADES

worksexception (instead)
Whenever you would play a Power Card, you may instead pay any amount of Energy onto the card to make it an impending card ( Impending), setting it aside out of play for use on a future turn. (It doesn't provide Elements. It's still your Power Card, so it can be forgotten while it's impending.)

Run: Seed 7: dance-ask yes -> make-impending dances quake -> impending-pay ... 0 -> energy-on dances quake 0; no `played`, so fire-elements 0 0 on turn 1. Seeds 1-4 decline: play-card dances quake 0, played, fire-elements 0 1.

'would play ... instead' is an exception on the base `play-card` episode, so the cost payment is skipped too. 'You may' can't live inside an exception (they intercept unconditionally within their context), so the decision is a choice in an earlier `choose-cards` step, and the exception's context starts after a 'yes'. That requires the base to split 'decide which cards' from 'play them'. 'Doesn't provide Elements' needs no rule, because Elements are counted from `played` tuples. 'Any amount' is a choice over a 0..Energy js generator. Forgetting an impending card is not modeled.

RHYTHMIC POWER BUILDS TO A CATACLYSMIC CRESCENDO

workstrigger (after/when)
When you gain Energy from your Presence Track, also gain ? Energy onto each Power Card made Impending on a previous turn. If any Impending now have Energy on them at least equal to their cost, discard that Energy and play them. (This costs no card plays.)

Run: Seed 8: 3 Energy put on Quake (cost 4), +1 on turn 2 -> crescendo-play dances quake 1, played, used-on-turn dances quake 1. Seed 14: 2 + 1 + 1 -> crescendo-play on turn 2 (third turn). Seed 7: 0 + 1 + 1 stays impending. Once played, no further feeding.

The wiki text lost the printed per-turn amount to a template glitch ([{{{width}}}px]); 1 is assumed. 'Previous turn' needs turn numbers (impending S P M with M < current). 'Discard that Energy' is implicit, since the card leaves `impending`. Played cards never leave `in-play` (no Time Passes discard in core).

Rulebook machinery added alongside: Multiple turns (turns-done counter), Energy as @sum with negative spends, Spirit Phase steps gain-energy (from a track value fact) / choose-cards / play-cards with turn-keyed play-card episodes that pay their cost, js-defs plus/neg/upto.

  • Optional replacement ('you may instead') can't be an exception by itself, because exceptions are unconditional in their context; the choice must be made in an ordered earlier step and scope the exception, so the base has to separate deciding from doing.
  • `>play-card` / `>gain-energy-phase` without a turn key would also match earlier turns' episodes; every per-turn episode got a turn-number argument.
  • 'Any amount of Energy' needs a js generator (`upto`) as the choice domain.

Language findings

These are the problems that came up across many spirits, ranked by how often they decided a rule's status.

1. Simultaneous firings can't see each other

Rules that fire at the same moment run as siblings, and none sees the others' effects. This produced wrong results in at least six places:

  • Two Ravages missed a Blight cascade (base rules).
  • Two Dahan moved by one Push both took the same Presence (Thunderspeaker, Sharp Fangs).
  • Per-Dahan firings destroyed the same Presence twice (Sworn to Victory).
  • Two Blight additions in one land destroyed the same Presence (Finder).
  • Damage to the land and to Dahan ran in parallel, so “Dahan present” couldn't see the Ravage's kills (Hearth-Vigil).

Every fix was the same: a hand-written loop that picks one item, acts on it, then continues.

2. There is no Action

The rulebook counts and groups by Action: “max. once per Action” (Shifting Memory), “if you add multiple Presence at the same time, only once” (Heart of the Wildfire), “your Actions” (Wandering Voice), and “Spirit effects” (Destructive Nature).

Turn has no Action to key on, and episode ids can't be bound. Where it worked, it was because the effect ran inside a named episode (use-power S P), which also gave “who did it” for free (Responsibilities to the Dead).

3. Exceptions are always on

“You may … instead” cannot be one exception. Once installed it always replaces, and declining by re-emitting the original gets intercepted again and loops. Every optional rule asks first, in an earlier step, and installs the exception only on yes (Choke the Land, Dance of Decades).

A related problem: an exception can't be partly undone. Vengeance lets a Build happen that Disease already consumed, and had to restate the base Build rules to do it.

4. Exceptions catch their own output

A replacement that matches its own pattern loops (Badlands). One that re-emits the same relation with arguments outside the pattern is fine (Fathomless Mud). Several rules avoided re-triggering by using a lower-level verb, for example adding the Strife piece directly instead of “add Strife”. That works, but any other “when Strife is added” rule then can't see it.

5. Silent timing mistakes

The most expensive category, because nothing reports an error:

  • The rest of a rule runs inside the episode it matched, so it can't see facts that start when that episode ends (Lightning).
  • P, >q matches every earlier q, including other turns' and other offers' (Dances, Behemoth, Keeper).
  • Top-level facts never join episodes inside the game (Ocean).
  • A fact asserted from a rule anchored on another forever-fact floats where later reads can't see it (Towering Roots, Wounded Waters).
  • A ^ inside a short sub-episode is gone before its parent reads it (Shifting Memory).
  • A choice with no options quietly resolves to nothing (Breath of Darkness, Green).
  • A head variable not bound in the body becomes a fresh object (Keeper).

6. Nothing can stop being true

Tuples only grow, and turn-scoped facts need a turn key that episode ids can't supply. So these could not be expressed directly:

  • “Until changed” (Open the Ways).
  • Removing a card from a set (Days That Never Were).
  • “While the Incarna is here” as a standing guard (Heart-Tree).

Things that change were modeled as pieces at locations, which works well. Healing had to become an explicit event so it could be intercepted (Slow and Silent Death).

7. No negation, little arithmetic

Leaving things out by default is often free. The Endless Dark is “not a land” just by having no land row (Breath of Darkness). But other phrases needed workarounds:

  • “Inland”, “without Fire” and “not a Sacred Site” needed zero rows or extra board data.
  • Removing an explore source was impossible (Isolate).
  • Clamps like “min. 1 Health” aren't additive (Blistering Heat).
  • Symbol inequality, addition, subtraction and halving were all hand-written #js-defs.

8. Bugs found in the base slice

The forks found bugs in core.t itself:

  • Adding Presence moves every Presence in the supply, not one.
  • There is no Blight supply or loss condition, so cascades between two blighted lands can recurse until the step limit.
  • Blight's Presence destruction and cascade run as siblings.
  • The “ravaged” marker never resets, so later turns never Ravage.

None of these were fixed during the study, so every result was measured against the same base.

Every issue reported, by spirit

  • A rule's continuation runs inside the episode it first matched, so reads there cannot see facts that start when that episode ends; nothing warns about it (fix: `parent, >ep, ...`). Lightning's Swift Strike
  • No negative-number literal arithmetic: paying K Energy needs `minus 0 K NK` then a contribution of NK (a #js-def), since @sum is the only accumulator. Shadows Flicker Like Flame
  • Range comparison over Peano needs a bounded recursive acc (`within`); numeric ranges would need a numeric BFS in JS. Shadows Flicker Like Flame
  • Exceptions are unconditional: 'you may prevent it' must be decided by a choice placed before the intercepted tuple is emitted; deciding inside the replacement cannot fall back to the original (re-emission is re-intercepted). A Spread of Rampant Green
  • A choice domain derived from an acc that depends on the choice's own follow-up episode is silently empty (my first yes-no acc keyed on choke-ask): the choice resolves to nothing with no warning. A Spread of Rampant Green
  • 'For each X, do Y (choosing)' as parallel firings lets choices at the same moment collide; needs a sequential counted loop (or a builtin 'for each, one at a time'). Thunderspeaker
  • 'After episode E' via `parent, >E` runs concurrently with whatever the base starts after E; to run strictly before the next base step one must hook inside E after its known last sub-step (`E, >last-step`) -- there is no 'at the end of E, still inside E' form. Thunderspeaker
  • Simultaneous moves (one Push of several pieces) are sibling episodes, so per-move triggers can't see each other's effects (Ally of the Dahan moved one Presence twice). Thunderspeaker
  • Exception RHS may only use the intercepted tuple's variables, so context (which Spirit's Power) must be re-derived in a helper rule; with two copies of a Spirit this would be ambiguous. Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares
  • Top-level `+` facts sit on a branch unordered with the game and silently never join with episodes inside it; they must live in setup. Ocean's Hungry Grasp
  • No way to express an option available "at any time". Ocean's Hungry Grasp
  • `turn, >move P L` floats: it is after the move but unordered relative to the following phases, so effects can be invisible to the next phase; anchor triggers on a per-phase window instead. Keeper of the Forbidden Wilds
  • `phase, >move P L` alone fires once per later phase (>p only requires p to end before the window ends); restricting to the phase the move happened in needed a phase-scoped tag: `phase, (move P L), ..., ^tag` then `phase, tag, >move P L`. Keeper of the Forbidden Wilds
  • A head variable that is not bound in the body (I dropped S from the second rule) silently becomes a fresh object instead of an error (`forbidden-ground *8671 l3`). Keeper of the Forbidden Wilds
  • 'Not a Sacred Site' needs a complement; with no acc negation it is `presence-count S L N, lt N 2` plus explicit 0 rows. Keeper of the Forbidden Wilds
  • Reading a location 'after' a move from a sibling rule sees the pre-move value (the sibling is unordered with the moved fact); pass values from the triggering episode's arguments instead. Sharp Fangs Behind the Leaves
  • 'You may' needs an explicit `decline` option row in the choice domain each time. Sharp Fangs Behind the Leaves
  • core.t has no Blight supply / loss condition, so once all lands have Blight, cascades recurse forever (status: gas); this spirit's extra Blight makes that likely. A Blight supply limit would itself need an 'instead' exception whose context starts when the supply runs out. Heart of the Wildfire
  • Damage persisted as `+hit` facts never clears at Time Passes; per-turn damage needs a turn key. Heart of the Wildfire
  • 'At the same time' (one Action adding several Presence) has no handle: Turn has no notion of Action identity to dedupe triggers on. Heart of the Wildfire
  • A constraint that does not depend on the chosen value (under-limit S) still has to be written inside a `!(...)` that mentions the choice variable (`!(presence-dest S C, under-limit S)`). Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island
  • core's presence-choice moves every Presence in the supply (`presence-of S P, at P supply` is not a choice), so the scenario keeps one in supply; a real 'add a Presence from your track' needs its own choice. Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island
  • Distinguishing 'added by a Power' from 'added by this special rule' needs two verbs for the same physical act; a rule-provenance notion would be cleaner. Grinning Trickster Stirs Up Trouble
  • No symbol inequality builtin; `neq` via #js-def JSON comparison. Grinning Trickster Stirs Up Trouble
  • Energy can't go below zero only by convention: nothing stops a payment exceeding the total except a guard in each paying rule (`energy S E, ge E 1`). Grinning Trickster Stirs Up Trouble
  • No negation in acc bodies, so 'Inland' (= not coastal) had to be entered as data rather than derived. Lure of the Deep Wilderness
  • An anonymous inline choice (`?[rng] V, !(...), is V X` as in core's kill-invaders) cannot be narrowed by other rules; only choices that emit a naming tuple (like presence-choice / push-to) are extensible. Lure of the Deep Wilderness
  • No built-in inequality on symbols; needed `#js-def neq +A +B { if (JSON.stringify(A) !== JSON.stringify(B)) yield [] }`. Many Minds Move as One
  • Optional "counts as", chosen per Action, needs a choice at the start of every Action that reads the counted type, and there is no hook for that. Many Minds Move as One
  • `^x` emitted in a short sub-episode lives only there; effects meant for 'the rest of the Action' need `action, >sub, ^x`. Shifting Memory of Ages
  • No Action identity: 'max once per Action' can't be counted without explicitly threading an action key through every rule. Shifting Memory of Ages
  • Episodes that are 'Actions' are not distinguished from other episodes; rules like 'for a single Action' depend on the scenario wrapping things in an `action` episode. Shifting Memory of Ages
  • Core runs Blight's two consequences (destroy Presence, cascade) as sibling episodes, so a cascade that returns to the same land sees Presence that its sibling already destroyed: p1 was 'destroyed' 5 times in one run; core should sequence them (`~>destroy-presence…; ~cascade`). Stone's Unyielding Defiance
  • Core has no Blight supply, so once two adjacent lands are blighted the cascade can ping-pong indefinitely (bounded only by rng luck); real game ends by running out of Blight. Stone's Unyielding Defiance
  • Run hits gas from core's unbounded Blight cascades once l2 and l3 are both blighted (the collapse test adds Blight to l3); results above are from before gas. Volcano Looming High
  • Damage that lasts 'until end of turn' needs the `turn, >damage-mark P N, ^dmg P N` idiom because damage is dealt deep inside nested episodes; there is no way to name the turn directly. Volcano Looming High
  • Two encodings of 'damage lasts this turn' are incompatible: turn-scoped tuples (easy) cannot be extended past the turn, explicit heal events (interceptable) need every damage to persist; a base has to pick the interceptable one up front. Shroud of Silent Mist
  • No negation: 'without Fire', 'decline only if already legal' each need a positive or 0-default helper relation. Shroud of Silent Mist
  • Gathering 'one of your Presence' must be its own choice; matching `presence-of S X, at X From` moves all of them (core's presence-choice has this bug: it moves every Presence in the supply). Shroud of Silent Mist
  • An exception cannot be partially undone: once `{ build L => … }` has fired, the original tuple is gone, so an extension of the extension must re-implement the base effect (duplicating base rules). Vengeance as a Burning Plague
  • With core's unbounded cascades, any scenario where Ravage blights adjacent lands exhausts tuple-gas (50000 rows): acc rows multiply per moment. The test Defends the Ravage to stay under the limit. Vengeance as a Burning Plague
  • Sets that lose members (the Days set) can't be plain relations; anything removable must be modeled as a piece with an `at` location. Fractured Days Split the Sky
  • Choosing 'any card except the kept one' needs a JS `neq` over JSON-encoded terms. Fractured Days Split the Sky
  • run.sh's output filter hides any tuple whose name starts with `element`/`power`/`land`/`spirit`…; a report tuple named element-report silently vanished (renamed). Starlight Seeks Its Form
  • Counts read 'after' an action inside the same rule still see the value from the window start (le N 1 instead of N = 0), an easy off-by-one. Starlight Seeks Its Form
  • Per-phase loops ('during the Fast/Slow phase, repeatedly') need one continuation rule per phase and per non-decline option; a generic 'repeat until decline within the enclosing phase' form would collapse 4 rules to 1. Downpour Drenches the World
  • Two copies of the same fact (two Water icons on one card) can't be written as duplicate facts reliably; used one Water per card. Downpour Drenches the World
  • State kept in an episode vanishes when the episode ends (I first wrote `~energy-change finder 1`; the acc lost it); persistent resources must be `+` facts, and per-turn ones need `turn, >…, ^`. Finder of Paths Unseen
  • No retraction / 'until changed': a fact holds to top and a ^ tuple ends with its scope, so a toggleable state (Open the Ways) can only be approximated per turn; an @last relation can model 'current value' but not a set of tuples that other rules match directly (adjacent). Finder of Paths Unseen
  • Symbol inequality still needs a #js-def (neq) for 'two different lands'. Finder of Paths Unseen
  • Triggers on 'your Power does X' need X to be an episode carrying the actor; core's anonymous defend L N tuple was not enough, so the actor-tagged step had to be introduced in BASE-EXT. Eyes Watch from the Trees
  • Two Blight additions in parallel (the land's own Blight and a cascade into it) both read the same Presence at their start and both 'destroy' it (move q2 destroyed twice) instead of destroying two different Presence; same sibling-concurrency issue as the missed cascade. Workaround: serialize Blight additions (not done). Fathomless Mud of the Swamp
  • Recursive episodes nest (assign-damage inside assign inside assign-damage), so an outer episode is still alive during the inner step and an acc relation keyed only by land (assignable L V) mixed rows from D=2 and D=1; fix: key the acc row by every argument of the episode (assignable L D V). Rising Heat of Stone and Sand
  • Clamping a summed quantity (min. 1) cannot be expressed as another @sum contribution; needs a separate post-aggregation layer in the base. Rising Heat of Stone and Sand
  • `P, >q ...` matches any earlier q, not just ones inside P (>q needs no overlap): a re-offer rule `rises-offer S, >rises-choice S C, ~rises-offer S` matched choices from previous offers and looped until gas; nesting the re-offer inside the choice episode fixed it. Ember-Eyed Behemoth
  • Choice values that are compound terms (to l3) render as opaque refs (*6334) in output; reports have to destructure them. Ember-Eyed Behemoth
  • 'Once per turn' needs either negation or a counter; @sum with an explicit 0 row is the idiom (bool acc relations have no absent row to match). Ember-Eyed Behemoth
  • Sibling sub-episodes launched with plain `~a, ~b` from one rule body are concurrent, so a guard in b-triggered rules cannot see a's effects; ordering must be written into the base with `~>` (here: damage-dahan before damage-land). Hearth-Vigil
  • Hard-coded arithmetic in base rules (half D N) blocks additive modifiers; quantities like Health must be @sum relations from the start. Hearth-Vigil
  • Exceptions cannot filter on 'whose' a choice-based destroy is (destroy-presence carries an opaque choice term), so the exception intercepts the downstream `move X destroyed` with X bound in the context instead. Hearth-Vigil
  • 'When all X leave' needs grouping by action; Turn has no notion of an action boundary to aggregate moves over, so the trigger is per-move. Hearth-Vigil
  • No interval-valued state: 'while the Incarna is in L' cannot be an exception context, because location is an acc @last value (per-moment rows), not a tuple with an interval; guards are read once at context start. Towering Roots of the Jungle
  • Acc relations cannot trigger emissions, so 'the first time condition C becomes true' must be re-checked inside every episode that can change C. Towering Roots of the Jungle
  • A trigger anchored on a wide window (`game, >add-piece ... , +empowered I`) placed +empowered at a moment not ordered before the later build-step, so the Build-skip guard never saw it; anchoring the check inside the add-piece episode (`add-piece L vitality, >move V L, ...`) fixed it. Silent failure. Towering Roots of the Jungle
  • JS relations work inside acc bodies (used for bounded reach with plus/lt). Towering Roots of the Jungle
  • A choice with no options resolves to nothing silently, so 'if there is no legal destination, you lose' needs a separate @sum count of options with a 0 row. Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine
  • Helper views that range over all locations (land:invader-count via `at X L`) leak into non-lands; every rule about lands needs an explicit `land L` guard. Closed-world 'not a land' is otherwise a strength: most Endless Dark restrictions needed no rules. Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine
  • A test can narrow a rng choice with an extra `!` constraint read through the named choice tuple (`targeting S dread, (target-chosen S dread T), !(test-target T)`), which is a handy way to force scenarios. Breath of Darkness Down Your Spine
  • Arithmetic on costs (cost + previous uses) and spending needs #js-def plus/neg; Energy is an @sum with negative contributions. Relentless Gaze of the Sun
  • No per-phase 'after' anchor: `turn, >use-power ...` continues until end of turn, so to confine Repeats to the current phase you'd need one rule per phase (no variable over episode names). Relentless Gaze of the Sun
  • core's `move` has no actor/cause, so 'when your Actions move X' needs a separate cause-tagged episode (`action-move S I To`). Every move-triggered special rule would want core's move to carry its cause. Wandering Voice Keens Delirium
  • Isolate's 'not a source of Explorers' cannot be added: core's `explorable` is a union of positive acc rows and acc bodies have no negation, so an extension can't remove a source. Wandering Voice Keens Delirium
  • Blight cascade (core) can ping-pong forever between two blighted lands (no Blight supply/Blight Card), and sibling cascade/destroy-presence branches each move the same Presence to destroyed (seed 3 run). Wandering Voice Keens Delirium
  • An 'or' in rule text ('Explorer / Town') becomes a helper acc with one row-producing rule per alternative. Wandering Voice Keens Delirium
  • `>p` matches ANY earlier p, including previous turns' episodes (`spirit-phase, >play-cards` fired once per earlier turn); workaround: an explicit `after-...` step, or key the episode by turn number (`>healing-ask S H R N` with `turns-done N`). Wounded Waters Bleeding
  • A fact asserted by a rule anchored on another forever-fact (`claimed S H, ..., +rule-removed ...`) floats and wasn't visible to the next turn's exception; assert it inside a bounded episode (the seeking step) instead. Wounded Waters Bleeding
  • core is single-turn; multi-turn needs a counter and a `game, >turn, ... ~turn` rule. core's `+ravaged X -> 1` (#agg, to top) then leaks, so turns 2+ never Ravage. Wounded Waters Bleeding
  • Optional replacement ('you may instead') can't be an exception by itself, because exceptions are unconditional in their context; the choice must be made in an ordered earlier step and scope the exception, so the base has to separate deciding from doing. Dances Up Earthquakes
  • `>play-card` / `>gain-energy-phase` without a turn key would also match earlier turns' episodes; every per-turn episode got a turn-number argument. Dances Up Earthquakes
  • 'Any amount of Energy' needs a js generator (`upto`) as the choice domain. Dances Up Earthquakes

What to change

In the language

  1. Sequential iteration. A construct for “for each X (in an order the player chooses), do …”, written once instead of as a hand-rolled pick-next loop. The same construct would fix multi-piece moves and per-item triggers. Why: §1 simultaneity · Ravage cascade · Thunderspeaker · Sharp Fangs · Sworn to Victory · Finder · Hearth-Vigil
  2. Optional exceptions. {? p … => e}: ask a choice when the tuple is intercepted, and let a declined tuple pass through without being intercepted again. Why: §3 always on · Choke the Land · Dance of Decades · Vengeance
  3. Re-entrancy guard. A replacement is never intercepted by the exception that produced it, which would fix Badlands-style boosts. Why: §4 own output · Badlands · Fathomless Mud
  4. Actions as first-class. Bindable episode ids (or a built-in “current action root”), so “once per Action”, “at the same time” and “your Actions” have something to key on. Why: §2 no Action · Shifting Memory · Wildfire · Wandering Voice · Destructive Nature · Responsibilities to the Dead
  5. Lints for the silent traps. Warn on:
    • a rule that matches top-level facts;
    • >p where nothing bounds which p;
    • a choice whose options are always empty;
    • an unbound head variable;
    • a read inside an episode that only becomes visible after it ends.
    Why: §5 timing · Lightning · Dances · Behemoth · Keeper · Ocean · Towering Roots · Breath of Darkness · Green
  6. Interval-valued views. Turn a run of equal acc values (“the Incarna is in L”) into a tuple with an interval, usable as an exception context. Why: §6 nothing stops · Heart-Tree · Open the Ways
  7. Small built-ins. Symbol neq, integer arithmetic, and stratified negation in acc bodies. Why: §7 negation, arithmetic · Isolate · Blistering Heat · Breath of Darkness

In the way the rules are written

  • Every noun the rulebook uses gets a named view, and nothing reads it inline. Examples: land-for, terrain-for, sacred-site, beasts-at, speed, health, push-dest, presence-source.
  • Every quantity is a sum of contributions, each tagged with its cause.
  • Every verb is its own episode and carries its actor: move, add-blight, destroy, heal, build, add-strife, use-power, growth.
  • Every choice is named, so other rules can constrain it.
  • Steps the rulebook orders are ordered with ~>; nothing that can interact is left as siblings.
  • One shared library for the rulebook machinery the forks each rewrote (Energy, Damage and Health, Range, Growth, Events, Time Passes, turn numbers), so all 37 spirit files can load together.
